principles.text: Make an offer so good people feel stupid saying no. If not enough say yes, make the offer better.
Go all in on one avatar, one product, one channel. Splitting attention across ventures is the biggest founder mistake.
Find the one constraint by asking why you can't 10x each input, then work only on it until it's removed.
Get better, not bigger. A product that retains and earns referrals is what makes leads affordable.
Volatility is a symptom of insufficient volume. Do 100 reps, study the top 10%, and repeat.

sampleQA.question: How should I price my first offer?

answer.text: Start free or cheap to get flow, then raise the price 20% every five customers until conversion times price starts to drop.
Price on what the customer is willing to pay, not on what you feel you deserve.
If profit is thin, sell to richer customers or raise prices 2-10x, backed by faster delivery, a guarantee or more ease.
Never cut price to close a deal. Change terms, such as a payment plan, instead.

sampleQA.question: My business has plateaued. Should I start a new one?

answer.text: No. You carry your own ceiling into the next business; a $4M entrepreneur builds another $4M business.
Unless you've exhausted your total addressable market, a plateau means there's something you don't yet know how to do.
Ask a specific question like 'what's stopping us from $5M a month?' and reframe the gap as 'how do I...'.
Break the money-making system into input actions and ask why you can't 10x each one to locate the constraint.

sampleQA.question: How do I close more sales without rewriting my pitch?

answer.text: Contact leads within 60 seconds of opt-in; speed of response is the biggest lever on close rate.
Sell seven days a week. Adding weekends gives about 29% more selling days.
Route the best leads to the best closers instead of round-robin.
Raise show rates by maximizing availability, using short slots and booking same or next day.
